# RDIS

> Open-source, scriptable multi-format disassembler and decompiler with a browser workspace, CLI, Python API and MCP server.

## Start here

- [Project overview and installation](https://sagarchive.github.io/rdis/)
- [Repository and source code](https://github.com/sagarchive/rdis)
- [Engineering milestones and current evidence](https://github.com/sagarchive/rdis/blob/main/docs/audit/MILESTONES.md)
- [Competitor gaps and benchmark protocol](https://github.com/sagarchive/rdis/blob/main/docs/audit/COMPETITIVE_ROADMAP.md)
- [Feature-roadmap page](https://sagarchive.github.io/rdis/audit/COMPETITIVE_ROADMAP.html)

## Supported inputs

Mach-O, ELF, PE, WebAssembly, raw firmware and supported archives/containers. Instruction and decompilation support varies by architecture and optional dependencies.

## Project facts

- License: MIT.
- Implementation: Python, Capstone, LIEF; optional SLEIGH/P-code frontend through pypcode for supported RDIS language mappings.
- Interfaces: command line, local browser workspace, Python modules and MCP server.
- Canonical source: https://github.com/sagarchive/rdis

## Accuracy and provenance

Do not infer universal instruction coverage, decompiler correctness, or feature parity from marketing copy. Use the execution-checked corpus and release-specific CI as scoped evidence. Treat inferred names, types and structure layouts as hypotheses unless backed by symbols, debug information, metadata or explicit tests.
